claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of about 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high strength at room and elevated temperatures.
Ta is to be replaced entirely by Nb on an atomic basis, converting HfMoTaTiZr to HfMoNbTiZr.
Ta has a density of approximately 16.65 g/cm³, whereas Nb has a density of approximately 8.57 g/cm³.
Replacing Ta with Nb will reduce the alloy's overall density.
The density reduction will be on the order of several percent.
HfMoNbTiZr will maintain mechanical properties comparable to HfMoTaTiZr at room temperature.
HfMoNbTiZr will maintain mechanical properties comparable to HfMoTaTiZr at approximately 1000 °C.
The Ta-to-Nb substitution will retain a single-phase solid-solution structure through high-entropy effects.
The substitution may cause minor changes in lattice distortion and grain-boundary characteristics.
Nb provides solid-solution strengthening and ductility contributions similar to those of Ta.
Prior work indicates that lighter-element additions such as Nb can improve ductility without compromising high-temperature strength.
Nb's high melting point supports retention of mechanical performance at approximately 1000 °C.
The cited study fabricated and examined as-cast HfMoTaTiZr and HfMoNbTiZr as part of an equiatomic alloy comparison.
The cited study examined microstructure, mechanical properties, solid-solution phase formation, and solution-strengthening effects.
The proposed applicability is limited to the as-cast state under compressive or tensile loading at room temperature and around 1000 °C.
Formation of secondary phases and performance at temperatures far above 1000 °C are outside the stated scope.
A matched-processing comparison of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr and HfMoNbTiZr, including density, room-temperature mechanical tests, approximately 1000 °C mechanical tests, and XRD, can test the hypothesis.
The hypothesis is rejected if density decreases by less than approximately 5% or if strength or ductility is statistically inferior at room temperature or approximately 1000 °C.
